title: Step 4: Lifecycle: TTL, versioning, forget, consolidation
description:
Add lifecycle features to the repositories/MemoryStore from Step 3:
- `forget(id, scope)` — sets deleted_at (tombstone), never hard-deletes by
  default; add a separate `purge_expired()` maintenance method that hard-
  deletes rows past expires_at AND already soft-deleted, callable via a
  script/cron, not automatically.
- optimistic concurrency on `version` for updates (raise on stale write)
- a `Consolidator` protocol: a pluggable callback
  `(raw_memories: list) -> list[derived_memory]` that MemoryStore can
  invoke synchronously after writes to working/episodic memory, producing
  semantic facts / entity profile updates / procedural memory. Ship a
  no-op default consolidator plus a documented example of wiring in an
  LLM-based one. Make clear in docs how a caller would instead run this
  async (e.g. call it from a cron job reading unconsolidated rows) —
  implement the sync path now, just document the async extension point.

comments.text: Built BaseRepository.forget() (soft-delete tombstone; soft_delete() kept as alias), BaseRepository.update() (optimistic concurrency: WHERE version = record.version, raises StaleWriteError on 0 rowcount, atomically increments version), BaseRepository.purge_expired() (hard-DELETE WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL, scoped, never auto-called). Added Consolidator Protocol + NoOpConsolidator to types.py with full LLM-based wiring example in docstring. Added MemoryStore.remember() as primary write entry point (dispatches by model type, runs consolidator sync on working/episodic only, consolidator errors caught+logged never propagated). Added MemoryStore.forget(id, type, scope) facade and MemoryStore.purge_expired(scope) facade returning {table: count} dict. Added scripts/purge_expired.py (cron maintenance) and scripts/consolidate_pending.py (reference async polling pattern). Added StaleWriteError to exceptions.py, re-exported from store.py and __init__.py. 36 new unit tests (104 total). ruff clean, mypy strict clean.
